summary: Backend testing of BidBlitz POS Pro suite (pos_pro.py, 36 endpoints). 18/19 pytest tests PASSED. 1 endpoint (/api/pos/tse/sign-sale/{sale_id}) is MISSING from code despite being listed in the review request and referenced in a comment in pos_pro.py line 42. All other Pro features — GoBD integrity/archive, KDS stations+orders+status, QR table flow (enable + public lookup + public submit without auth), Pfand register/return/outstanding, AI Assistant (gpt-5.1 via Emergent LLM Key, real German answer returned), Product recognition (Gemini 2.5 Pro wired correctly — 200 on dummy base64), Dynamic Pricing (create/list/apply/delete), Customer Display (no auth), Stempeluhr (punch/me/store), Tips (add/distribute/my-payouts), Webhooks (CRUD + HMAC test fire), API keys (create/list/revoke) — all return 200 with expected payload shapes end-to-end against real MongoDB.

critical.issue: Endpoint returns 404 — handler is NOT implemented in pos_pro.py even though review request lists it and the module's top comment (line 42) advertises it. The extended pos_extended.py only has /tse/configure and /tse/sign-payment (operates on pos_payments, not pos_sales).

minor.issue: Date-range logic is convoluted (line 55: `(1 if not month and 12 == 12 else 0)` — the literal `12 == 12` is always True, so when month is None the end year becomes year+1 correctly, but the boolean expression is dead/unreadable and risks silent bugs when refactored). Works for the happy path but should be simplified.

When auto-creating KDS orders, uses `table['number']` (line 239) but schema elsewhere uses `table.get('name') or table.get('number')` — inconsistent. If `number` is missing the insert stores None. Low impact since submission still succeeds.
Hardcodes €1.00 for cup / €0.25 for anything else (line 293) when no deposit_id is passed. Should come from store config or deposits table.
Uses regex on ISO string to filter by day (`created_at: {$regex: ^YYYY-MM-DD}`). Works but is not index-friendly. Prefer range-match on ISO timestamps.

action_items: Implement the missing `POST /api/pos/tse/sign-sale/{sale_id}` endpoint in pos_pro.py. It should: (1) require merchant auth via _require_merchant, (2) fetch the sale, (3) reuse the TSE signing logic from pos_extended.py /tse/sign-payment but write `tse_signature`/`tse_signed_at` onto the pos_sales doc (so the `sales_signed` counter in /gobd/integrity-check works), (4) also append an entry to pos_gobd_archive for GoBD compliance.
Optional: simplify the gobd_list end-date computation (pos_pro.py line 55) — remove the `12 == 12` tautology.
Optional: align table-number field usage in public_order_submit KDS auto-creation (line 239).
critical_code_review_comments: pos_pro.py line 55 — end-date expression `year + (1 if not month and 12 == 12 else 0)` contains a tautology (`12 == 12`) and mixes two different conventions; replace with a clear if/else using dateutil.relativedelta or manual month-rollover.
pos_pro.py line 42 comment advertises `/tse/sign-sale` but no handler is defined — either implement it or remove the claim.
pos_pro.py `deposits/return` fallback pricing (line 293) hardcodes EU deposit rates (€1 cup, €0.25 bottle). Move to merchant/store config for DE-vs-AE flexibility.
pos_pro.py `assistant/ask` gathers heavy DB aggregations on every call (4 sequential queries) — consider caching the context summary per-merchant for 60s.
pos_pro.py `product_recognize` sends up to 80 product names as hint inside the system prompt — for large catalogs this inflates token count. Cap at 40 and include category.
pos_pro.py `tips/pool/distribute` uses regex on ISO string to filter by day — use a range match (`$gte` start-of-day, `$lt` next day ISO) for index usage.

pos_pro.py `pricing/apply` (line 479) uses `{'product_id': None, 'category': ...}` to match category-level rules — if a rule doc was inserted without `product_id` key at all, that match fails. Safer: `$or: [{product_id: pid}, {product_id: {$in: [null, None]}, category: cat}]` or store an explicit null.

pos_pro.py `create_pricing_rule` spreads `req.dict()` directly after setting `rule_id`/`store_id` — if a future PricingRule field is named `rule_id` or `store_id`, it would silently overwrite. Use req.dict(exclude={'rule_id','store_id'}).
pos_pro.py `test_webhook` stores `last_error[:200]` but does not clamp `last_status` types — low risk but worth noting.

success_rate.backend: 95% (18/19 endpoint tests passed; 1 endpoint is missing from code)

seed_data_creation: Created during tests: 1 TEST KDS station + 1 KDS order, 1 pro table + QR-enabled + 1 guest order (GST-…), 1 outstanding Pfand deposit (0.25 EUR bottle x3), 1 TEST Happy-Hour pricing rule (deactivated at end), 1 timeclock 'in' punch, 1 tip of €2.50, 1 TEST webhook (deactivated), 1 TEST API key (revoked). All TEST-prefixed / idempotent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run with `pytest backend/tests/test_pos_pro.py -v`. All endpoints use cookie session via /api/auth/login. If main agent implements /tse/sign-sale, the last failing test in TestTSESignSale will pass automatically. Pre-existing store STR-C433697A3B belongs to haendler@bidblitz.com — tests discover it dynamically via /api/pos/stores. The Emergent LLM Key is wired and functional for both gpt-5.1 (assistant) and gemini-2.5-pro (product recognition).
rca_of_the_issue: The /api/pos/tse/sign-sale/{sale_id} endpoint was planned (top-of-file comment at pos_pro.py line 42 explicitly states 'GoBD-archive + sign-sale') but the handler function was never added to the router. The GoBD integrity-check counts `pos_sales` with `tse_signature` field set, so without this sign-sale endpoint the `compliance_rate` will always be 0 for new sales — breaking the KassenSichV flow for the pos_sales path (pos_payments are covered by pos_extended.py /tse/sign-payment). Fix: add `@router.post('/tse/sign-sale/{sale_id}')` that mirrors pos_extended's /tse/sign-payment logic but on pos_sales and ALSO writes to pos_gobd_archive.
